title: Nobody named it — menopause silence across cultures (Nadia, 49)
caption:
Hot flashes ran a median 7.4 years in SWAN (JAMA Intern Med, 2015).
Log yours, then ask for a Menopause Society certified clinician.
Send this to the aunt who says it's nothing. What did your family call it?
www.aiforheratx.org
#menopause #perimenopause #womenshealth #hotflashes #midlifewomen

scenes.text: Year four of hot flashes. Nobody ever *named* it.
The group chat says everyone goes through it. Nobody says how *long* it lasts.
phrases: Don't make a big thing of it.
Nadia, 49: I soaked through my shirt in a standup today.
And I still haven't told a single person at work.

scenes.text: SWAN followed 3,302 women: hot flashes ran a median of 7.4 years, closer to 10 for Black women.

scenes.text: Anthropologist Margaret Lock found Japanese women called it *kōnenki* — a stage of life, not a disease.
phrases: Her doctor just said 'normal, at your age.'
Lock, 1993: in Japan it had a name and a place — kōnenki.
Different countries, same hush. Nadia stopped feeling rude for asking.

scenes.text: Log each flash — the time, what you were doing, how you slept — and take that page to an *MSCP* clinician.
phrases: Tonight: note each flash — time, what you were doing, how you slept.
This week: search the Menopause Society directory for an MSCP-certified clinician.
Daily after 51: 1,200 mg calcium (NIH ODS) and 150 minutes of moderate movement a week (WHO).
